- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is low, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- If recent price drop is followed by a spike, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast peak by 10–15% after spike.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true mean over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction (reduce by 2–5% per day).  
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.3–0.7), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., drop after peak), model often overshoots — cap forecast at 10% below peak.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -0.5 → +0.5), model tends to lag — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
